newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico left demands army pullout after rebel truce.
newsitem.headline: Mexico left demands army pullout after rebel truce.

text.p: Mexico's main leftist political party on Thursday demanded that the army pull out of the southern state of Guerrero in response to a ceasefire called by leftist guerrillas in the state.

The Democratic Revolution Party (PRD), which opposes armed struggle, said the move would help foster "a climate of peace" in municipal and state legislative elections due to be held in Guerrero on October 6.
"The government of President Ernesto Zedillo should pull out the Mexican army immediately," PRD spokeswoman Laura Itzel Castillo said in a statement.
Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrillas on Wednesday declared a month-long truce in Guerrero, saying it wanted to avoid disrupting the elections.
The EPR first appeared in Guerrero state on June 28, and two months later hit police and military targets in several states in a wave of attacks that caused at least 20 deaths.
Thousands of government troops have poured into Guerrero since the group's appearance.

The National Intermediation Commission, which is helping mediate peace talks between the government and Zapatista rebels in the southern state of Chiapas, called this week for talks between the government and the EPR.
But the government has accused the EPR of "terrorism" and rejects talks with them. The Zapatistas say they have nothing to do with the EPR and have asked them to stay out of Chiapas.
